CIEEDAC (2000). Industrial Energy End-use Analysis (Canada). Report prepared by M.K. Jaccard and Associates and Willis Energy Services Ltd for Natural Resources Canada; Canadian Industrial Energy End-use Data and Analysis Centre (CIEEDAC), Simon Fraser University, Burnaby, BC, September 2000. 446 pp. No DOI or report number printed. Author attribution on the title page not verified (the PDF text starts at the Executive Summary; running footer reads "M.K. Jaccard and Associates / Willis Energy Services Ltd.").

Locators are printed page numbers (chapter-page, e.g. 7-44; PDF page = ordinal in the 446-page file, App. 7.1b is PDF p.379). The report (M.K. Jaccard and Associates with Willis Energy Services Ltd for Natural Resources Canada; ISTUM end-use model) is the heritage technology database of the CIMS lineage: Appendix x.1b of Chapters 3-8 and Appendix 2.2 give, per ISTUM technology code, energy per unit of service (GJ/t, GJ/m3, GJ per GJ steam), capital cost and O&M for a small and a large plant (1990 dollars) and life. Data are Canadian, base year 1990. Targeted pass of 106 technologies: chemicals (chlor-alkali, chlorate, peroxide, ammonia/methanol, ethylene, polymers, caustic evaporation), iron and steel (sinter, 6 whole routes, ladle, EAF, casting, reheating, rolling, annealing, oxygen), pulp and paper (digesters, mechanical pulp, deinking, bleaching, dryers, evaporators, lime kilns, recovery boilers, paper machine), refining (distillation, FCC, hydrocracking, hydrotreating, alkylation, isomerization, reforming), cement and lime kilns and mills, selected mining and oil-sands steps, and boilers/cogeneration from Chapter 2. Not loaded: the other ISTUM variants (control/heat-recovery option codes, oil-fired twins), motors, pumps, fans, compressors, lighting and HVAC (generic auxiliaries), debarking/chipping, the Appendix c technology stocks except chlor-alkali, the scenario results. Rules used: each row gives energy coefficients by carrier (electricity columns summed with the formula shown; negative = produced); capital and O&M per annual unit of capacity are loaded as a min-max range between the small and large plant (no central value), lifetime as printed. Costs are 1990 dollars, currency presumed Canadian; COST BASIS NOT STATED. Energy is final energy; heating-value basis is not stated for fuels. Traps: (1) Chlor-alkali Appendix 7.1b prints a column headed Steam (18.07, 14.91, 13.55, 22.13, 10.83) that equals 1.294 x the direct electricity in every row; it was not loaded (other-values). Energy is per MECU (1 t chlorine + 1.12 t caustic soda); off-gas credit -3.90 GJ/MECU is a flow. (2) Ammonia, methanol and the combined plant carry identical coefficients (0.60 electricity, 30.14 natural gas): generic, feedstock treatment not stated. (3) Mining table capital and O&M are placeholder-like (46,000/115,000 repeated) and not loaded; oil-sands and crude-oil costs likewise. (4) Evaporator, lime-kiln (kraft), recovery-boiler and black-liquor tables have unclear capacity bases and no costs loaded; refining caps are printed with small larger than large for several tables (as printed). (5) Several tables print energy under a header that does not line up with the blank columns (refinery FCC, reheating furnaces, paper dryers); I assigned by column position and noted it; PU DR NG/RE (gas and oil pulp dryers) print no fuel use and were skipped. (6) Page 6-10 header says GJ per tonne of steel for the refinery hydrogen table (typo); hydrogen plant and sulfur rows were skipped. (7) Capital cost at both sizes is identical for ethylene crackers although capacity differs 2.5x. (8) Two draft versions exist (chemicals PDF dated 13 Sep 2000 vs full report 28 Sep 2000); text identical apart from the table of contents. (9) Text figures in Chapter 7 (Table 7.1 Canadian average intensities) are in other-values, not technology rows.
